title: Teaching & Data Work
text:
This section presents my experience in university teaching, research assistance, and quantitative data work across education, sociology, psychology, and social policy projects.




Universidad Alberto Hurtado (2025–present)
Instructor for undergraduate students in Science Education. The course covers descriptive statistics, probability, data visualization, and introductory quantitative reasoning for future science teachers.



Universidad San Sebastián (2015–2021)
Instructor in undergraduate psychology courses, including:

Foundations of Socioanthropological Approaches to Human Behavior
Qualitative Research Methods
Community Psychology
Social Psychology
Undergraduate thesis and capstone assessment

These courses connected theoretical perspectives with practical research and intervention skills.



Universidad del Desarrollo (2015–2017)
Instructor in professional development courses for psychology students, emphasizing:

Scientific writing
Research project design
Evidence-based argumentation
Interdisciplinary problem solving







Wealth and Social Cohesion from a Relational Perspective (2025–present)
Funded by the Volkswagen Foundation through the ISI-LMU Munich project.
My doctoral dissertation examines household wealth configurations, economic security, and educational inequality in Chile. The project combines survey data, administrative records, and quantitative methods to study how wealth shapes life opportunities and educational trajectories.



Princeton University (2024–2025)
Data analyst for the project Intergenerational Mobility in Latin America: Patterns and Trends.
Responsibilities included:

Statistical processing of large-scale datasets
Data harmonization and management
Quantitative analysis of educational and mobility indicators
Documentation and reproducible workflows




Millennium Nucleus LM2C2 (2024–2025)
Research assistant for database construction and quantitative analysis.
Responsibilities included:

Database construction
Data cleaning and integration
Statistical analysis
Research support for publications and reports

title: Gonzalo Torres Rosales
section: Social Inequality, Well-Being, and Quantitative Social Research
text:
Social Inequality, Well-Being, and Quantitative Social Research
I am a Social Psychologist and PhD Candidate in Sociology at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile. My research focuses on social inequality, economic well-being, and the conditions that shape life opportunities across the life course. I am particularly interested in how wealth, economic security, and educational trajectories interact to reproduce—or mitigate—social disadvantage.
My work is fundamentally interdisciplinary. I draw on perspectives from sociology, psychology, and economics to understand how structural conditions and individual experiences jointly shape human development and social outcomes. Methodologically, I specialize in quantitative social research, combining survey data, administrative records, longitudinal designs, and computational approaches to study complex social processes.
Beyond academia, my research agenda has been shaped by direct experience in civil society organizations, educational projects, and applied policy research. These experiences have reinforced my interest in producing knowledge that is both analytically rigorous and socially consequential. Across my work, I seek to contribute to a better understanding of the mechanisms that generate inequality and to inform debates about how societies can expand opportunities, security, and well-being.

Core areas

Social inequality and economic well-being
Wealth, economic security, and educational trajectories
Quantitative methods, survey data, and administrative records
Interdisciplinary social science across sociology, psychology, and economics

title: Beyond Research
text:
My work extends beyond academic research. Over the last decade, I have worked across civil society organizations, consulting, public policy, and public writing, developing applied knowledge on education, poverty, work, and social inequality.




Fundación INFOCAP (2018–2024)
I worked in research and institutional development in a civil society organization focused on labor training, education, and social inclusion. My work included internal and external analysis, institutional development proposals, research reports, and evidence-based support for programs addressing vulnerability, work, and adult education.






United Nations Development Programme, Chile
Independent consultant for the analysis of the Social Well-Being Survey of the Ministry of Social Development and Family, using advanced quantitative methods.



Ministry of Education, Chile — FONIDE 2023
Technical evaluator for proposals submitted to the Education Research and Development Fund. The evaluation considered methodological quality, internal coherence, and alignment with public policy priorities in education.



National Council for Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation for Development (Consejo CTCI), 2025
Author of the report Recommendations of the CTCI Council in Higher Education: A Systematization of Contributions from Recent Decades, focused on synthesizing policy recommendations in higher education, science, technology, knowledge, and innovation.
Report available here






I have written public-facing opinion columns on poverty, adult education, lifelong learning, inequality, and institutional development, mainly in El Mostrador. These pieces reflect my interest in connecting social research with public debate.
Selected columns include:

Avanzar hacia una institucionalidad chilena para el Aprendizaje a lo largo de toda la vida (2023)
Mejores definiciones de la pobreza para mejores soluciones a los problemas de Chile (2022)
Educación de adultos como un eje central para el desarrollo socioeconómico del país post-pandemia (2022)
El nepotismo, un problema complejo: educación, equidad y redes (2018)








Development and evaluation of projects aimed at expanding training opportunities for people facing socioeconomic vulnerability.



Applied work on adult education, employability, and institutional development for lifelong learning.



Participation in initiatives connecting labor training, digital inclusion, and renewable energy skills.

title: Gonzalo Torres Rosales
section: Sociología de la riqueza, desigualdad y trayectorias educativas
text:
Sociología de la riqueza, desigualdad y trayectorias educativas
Soy candidato a doctor en Sociología en la Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile. Mi investigación examina cómo la riqueza de los hogares, la deuda y la seguridad económica configuran trayectorias educativas desiguales en Chile.
Mi trabajo estudia la riqueza no solo como un stock de recursos, sino como una configuración de activos, pasivos, liquidez, colateral y seguridad intertemporal.

Agenda de investigación

Configuraciones de riqueza: activos y deudas como formas estructuradas de ventaja y vulnerabilidad.
Seguridad económica: cómo los hogares gestionan incertidumbre, shocks y decisiones orientadas al futuro.
Desigualdad educativa: cómo la riqueza y la seguridad moldean trayectorias escolares y universitarias.



Proyectos actuales

Configuraciones patrimoniales y la desigual seguridad de los futuros familiares en Chile
Reconstrucción de riqueza mediante encuestas y machine learning
Hardship económico subjetivo en Chile utilizando EBS 2023

title: Research
text:
Articles under review

Profiles of Attachment and Teacher Well-being: A Latent Class and Mediation Analysis
Authors: Paulina Guzmán M.; Jorge Varela T.; Gonzalo Torres-Rosales; Joaquín Cortés; Roy Hidalgo C.
Status: Submitted manuscript
This article examines profiles of attachment and teacher well-being using latent class and mediation analysis. It contributes to research on educational psychology, teacher well-being, and psychosocial mechanisms in school contexts.


Debt, Age, and the Conversion Gap in Subjective Economic Hardship: Evidence from Chile
Authors: Joaquín Prieto; Gonzalo Torres-Rosales
Status: Submitted manuscript
This article studies how debt, age, income position, and housing tenure shape subjective economic hardship in Chile. The paper examines the gap between objective socioeconomic location and subjective experiences of economic vulnerability.

title: Research
text:
Conference papers and presentations

How does vulnerability to poverty affect subjective well-being? A secure middle-class perspective for Chile
Authors: Joaquín Prieto; Gonzalo Torres
Presented at: ECINEQ 2025, 11th Conference of the Society for the Study of Economic Inequality, Washington, DC
This paper examines how vulnerability to poverty affects subjective well-being from the perspective of middle-class security in Chile.

title: Research
text:
Ongoing manuscripts

Household Wealth, Data Fragmentation, and Educational Stratification: A Survey-to-Administrative Strategy from Chile
Author: Gonzalo Torres-Rosales
Status: Doctoral thesis article / working paper
This article develops a strategy for incorporating household wealth into the study of educational stratification in contexts where administrative education records do not directly observe assets and debts. Using Chile as a strategic case, the paper proposes a survey-to-administrative approach to reconstruct functional indicators of household wealth and examine their relevance for educational inequality.


Economic Security Beyond Socioeconomic Status: Objective Position, Subjective Vulnerability, and Mental Health
Authors: Gonzalo Torres-Rosales; Cristóbal Cabezas
Status: Working paper
This article examines the relationship between objective socioeconomic position, subjective vulnerability, and mental health. It contributes to debates on economic security by distinguishing conventional socioeconomic status from subjective experiences of insecurity and psychological well-being.

title: Research
text:
Broader research interests


Social inequality and well-being
I study how social and economic inequalities shape subjective well-being, mental health, and life opportunities.


Wealth and economic security
My doctoral work focuses on wealth, debt, economic insecurity, and educational stratification.


Quantitative and computational methods
I work with survey data, administrative records, longitudinal designs, latent class analysis, and prediction-based measurement strategies.
